newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen taking a hit on red chip concerns.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen taking a hit on red chip concerns.

text.p: Hong Kong shares are expected to take another hit on Tuesday, with sentiment again affected by China's move to clamp down on red chips and uncertainty over property measures expected by Hong Kong's future government.
But the Dow industrials' 192.25-point fall overnight should have a limited impact on the market, which may ignore Wall Street during this last week of colonial rule, brokers said.

"The market will open weak, not because of Wall Street but because of the red chip measures and the measures expected to be introduced soon in Hong Kong regarding asset (property) prices," said Steven Thompson, chief analyst at Nikko Securities.
On Monday, the Hang Seng Index dropped 133.13 points to 15,021.23. Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks in London fell 2.19 points to 15,019.04.
"The Hang Seng is likely to fall between 100 and 200 points today to below the 15,000 level," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
But he said profit-taking pressure could be limited by continued heavy liquidity flows into the market and a positive underlying tone.
